examples.ko: 뉴스에서 극악한 범죄 소식을 들으면 마음이 무거워요.
examples.en: When I hear news of a heinous crime, my heart feels heavy.
The villain in that movie is truly atrocious.

examples.ko: 극악한 사기를 친 사람들이 결국 잡혔어요.
examples.en: The people who ran that vicious scam were finally caught.

examples.ko: 어떻게 그렇게 극악한 짓을 할 수 있어요?
examples.en: How could anyone do something so heinous?

examples.ko: 사람들은 극악한 범인에게 엄한 벌을 원했어요.
examples.en: People wanted a harsh punishment for the heinous offender.

examples.ko: 이야기 속 계모는 아이에게 극악하게 굴어요.
examples.en: The stepmother in the story treats the child in a cruel way.

explain: '나쁘다'보다 훨씬 강해서 뉴스나 글에서 범죄나 행동이 끔찍할 때 써요. '극악무도하다'처럼 한 덩어리로도 써요. 말할 때는 '끔찍하다'나 '잔인하다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '나쁘다' (bad) and is used in news and writing when a crime or an act is appalling. It also appears as a set phrase, '극악무도하다'. In speech people tend to say '끔찍하다' or '잔인하다' instead.

examples.ko: 약을 잘못 먹으면 극약이 될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you take medicine the wrong way, it can become a deadly poison.

examples.ko: 이 농약은 극약이니까 아이 손이 닿지 않게 두세요.
examples.en: This pesticide is a deadly poison, so keep it out of children's reach.

examples.ko: 극약 표시가 있는 병은 절대 만지지 마세요.
examples.en: Never touch a bottle that has a deadly poison label.

examples.ko: 그 약은 극약이라서 의사만 다룰 수 있어요.
examples.en: That drug is a deadly poison, so only doctors can handle it.

examples.ko: 할머니는 극약 같은 약은 집에 두지 않으세요.
examples.en: My grandmother doesn't keep dangerous drugs like that at home.

examples.ko: 위기를 넘기려고 회사가 극약 처방을 내렸어요.
examples.en: To get through the crisis, the company took drastic measures.

explain: '독약'과 비슷하지만 '극약 처방'처럼 위기에서 쓰는 마지막 수단을 비유할 때 많이 나와요. 실제 위험한 물질을 말할 때는 '독극물'도 같이 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: The company took drastic measures to survive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 효과가 클 수도 있지만 위험도 큰, 최후의 과감한 해결책을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a bold last-resort fix that may work well but carries big risks.

explain_en: It is close to '독약' (poison), but it often appears in the figurative '극약 처방', a last-resort measure in a crisis. For real dangerous substances, it is also useful to know '독극물' (toxic substance).

examples.ko: 그는 화가 나서 부모님께 극언을 했어요.
examples.en: He got angry and said harsh things to his parents.
There are many comments full of harsh words on the internet.

examples.ko: 아무리 화가 나도 극언은 삼가는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: No matter how angry you are, it is better to avoid extreme words.
The controversy grew because of the politician's harsh remarks.

examples.ko: 친구에게 극언을 듣고 한참 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: I heard harsh words from a friend and felt hurt for a long time.
Once you say really harsh things, it gets hard to make up.

explain: '막말'이나 '독설'과 비슷하지만 '극언'은 주로 글이나 뉴스에서 써요. '극언을 하다/삼가다/퍼붓다'처럼 함께 쓰는 말이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '심한 말'이라고 해도 충분해요.
explain_en: It is close to '막말' (rude talk) or '독설' (venom), but '극언' is mostly seen in writing and news. It pairs with verbs like '하다', '삼가다' and '퍼붓다'. In everyday talk, '심한 말' is enough.

examples.ko: 그 나라에서는 극우파의 목소리가 커지고 있어요.
examples.en: In that country, the voice of the far right is getting louder.

examples.ko: 극우파 정당이 선거에서 많은 표를 얻었어요.
examples.en: A far-right party won many votes in the election.
The far right and the far left clashed fiercely in the debate.
That reporter covered a far-right gathering.
Far-right supporters held a rally in the street.
I read an article criticizing the far right in the news.

explain: '극우'는 정치적으로 아주 오른쪽 입장이고, 반대말은 '극좌'예요. '파'는 그런 생각을 가진 무리를 말해서 '극우 세력', '극우 정당'처럼도 써요. 정치 기사에서 많이 보는 말이에요.
explain_en: '극우' is a very right-wing position, and its opposite is '극좌'. '파' means a group sharing that view, so you also see '극우 세력' and '극우 정당'. You will meet it mostly in political news.

examples.en: I speak to my grandfather using the highest honorific forms.
In old dramas, people used the highest honorifics to the king.

examples.ko: 극존칭이 너무 어려워서 외국인 친구가 힘들어해요.
examples.en: My foreign friend struggles because the highest honorifics are so hard.
In an interview, natural polite speech is better than extreme honorifics.

examples.ko: 이 말은 극존칭이라서 어른께 조심해서 써야 해요.
examples.en: This is an extremely honorific word, so use it carefully with elders.
The company notice is full of highly honorific expressions.

explain: 높임을 가장 높게 하는 느낌의 말이라서 보통 존댓말보다 더 격식 있고 조심스러운 표현에 써요. 친구 사이에 쓰면 어색하니까 상황을 잘 봐야 해요. '높임말', '존댓말'은 일상에서 더 넓게 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It describes the very highest level of respect, more formal and careful than ordinary polite speech. Using it among friends would sound odd, so watch the situation. '높임말' and '존댓말' are the broader everyday terms.

examples.en: That group is known as part of the far left.

examples.ko: 극좌파의 주장은 너무 극단적이라는 비판을 받았어요.
examples.en: The far left's claims were criticized as too extreme.
I saw a far-left group's protest on the news.

examples.ko: 그 정치인은 극좌파라고 불리는 것을 싫어해요.
examples.en: That politician dislikes being called far left.

examples.ko: 극좌파와 극우파는 서로 대화를 거의 안 해요.
examples.en: The far left and the far right hardly talk to each other.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 극좌파가 나온 배경을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, we learned the background of how the far left emerged.

explain: '극좌'는 정치적으로 아주 왼쪽 입장이고, 반대말은 '극우'예요. '극좌파'는 그런 입장을 가진 사람이나 무리를 말하고, 상대를 비난할 때 쓰는 말투가 되기도 해서 조심해서 써요. 뉴스나 토론에서 주로 봐요.
explain_en: '극좌' is a very left-wing position, and its opposite is '극우'. '극좌파' means the people or group holding it, and it can sound like an accusation, so use it carefully. You will see it mostly in news and debates.

examples.ko: 극지방은 일 년 내내 아주 추워요.
examples.en: The polar regions are very cold all year round.
The ice in the polar regions is gradually melting.
I watched a documentary about animals living in the polar regions.
The researchers left for an expedition to the polar regions.
In the polar regions, the night can last a very long time.
Someday I want to see the aurora in the polar regions.

explain: 북극과 남극 주변 지역을 함께 부르는 말이에요. 한쪽만 말할 때는 '북극', '남극'이라고 해요. 뉴스나 과학 수업에서 기후변화 이야기와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a collective name for the areas around the North and South Poles. When you mean just one, say '북극' or '남극'. It often comes up in news and science class together with climate change.

examples.en: My mother treats guests with great hospitality.
The staff at this restaurant give extremely attentive service.
Thanks to the devoted nursing, I recovered quickly.
I grew up receiving my grandmother's wholehearted love.

examples.ko: 아들의 효성이 극진하다고 동네에서 소문이 났어요.
examples.en: Word spread around the neighborhood that the son is deeply devoted to his parents.

examples.ko: 예의가 극진해서 몸 둘 바를 몰랐어요.
examples.en: They were so courteous that I didn't know where to put myself.

explain: 정성이 아주 깊고 대접이나 보살핌이 빈틈없을 때 써요. '극진한 대접', '극진한 간호', '극진한 사랑'처럼 명사 앞에서 많이 써요. '정성스럽다'보다 더 지극한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used when care or hospitality is extremely sincere and thorough. It often comes before a noun, as in '극진한 대접', '극진한 간호' and '극진한 사랑'. It feels stronger than '정성스럽다' (careful, sincere).

examples.en: I have a friend who takes devoted care of his parents.

examples.ko: 엄마가 몸살을 앓는 동안 아버지는 엄마를 극진히 간호했어요.
examples.en: While Mom was sick with aches, Dad nursed her devotedly.
The owner welcomed us warmly and with great care.
The hotel staff look after guests with great attention.

examples.ko: 극진히 대접받아서 몸 둘 바를 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I was treated so lavishly that I didn't know how to react.

examples.ko: 선생님이 병든 저를 극진히 보살펴 주셨어요.
examples.en: My teacher took devoted care of me when I was ill.

explain: '모시다, 대접하다, 간호하다, 보살피다'처럼 사람을 정성껏 돌보는 말과 잘 어울려요. '정성껏'보다 더 깊고 예의 바른 느낌이라 어른이나 손님에게 하는 일에 써요. 형용사 '극진하다'의 부사형이에요.
explain_en: It goes well with verbs of caring for people, such as '모시다', '대접하다', '간호하다' and '보살피다'. It feels deeper and more courteous than '정성껏', so it suits things done for elders or guests. It is the adverb form of '극진하다'.

examples.en: My parents lived thriftily their whole lives.
I bought a house with the money I saved by living frugally.
In a recession, everyone has to be frugal.

examples.ko: 근검절약하는 습관은 어릴 때부터 길러야 해요.
examples.en: You should build the habit of thrift from childhood.
Even after becoming rich, he stayed frugal.
To save money, I bring a packed lunch.

explain: '근검절약'은 '근검절약 정신', '근검절약을 실천하다'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요. 가훈이나 표어에 자주 나오는 말이라 조금 딱딱하게 들리고, 일상에서는 '아끼다', '절약하다'를 더 편하게 말해요. 반대말은 '낭비하다'예요.
explain_en: '근검절약' is also used as a noun, as in '근검절약 정신' and '근검절약을 실천하다'. It often shows up in family mottos and slogans, so it sounds a bit stiff; in daily talk, '아끼다' and '절약하다' are more casual. The opposite is '낭비하다' (to waste).

examples.en: I am barely getting by on my salary.
The shop has no customers, so it is barely hanging on.
I scraped together my tuition with part-time jobs.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 적자 속에서도 근근이 문을 열고 있어요.
examples.en: That company is barely staying open despite running at a loss.

examples.ko: 근근이 모은 돈을 병원비로 다 썼어요.
examples.en: I spent all the money I had barely saved up on hospital bills.

examples.ko: 할머니는 작은 밭에서 나온 것으로 근근이 먹고 사셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother barely got by on what came from her small field.

explain: '겨우', '간신히'와 비슷하지만 '근근이'는 어려운 형편에서 힘들게 이어 가는 모습에 많이 써요. '살다, 버티다, 모으다, 이어 가다'와 잘 어울려요. '합격선을 근근이 넘다'처럼 한 번에 아슬아슬하게 해내는 일에는 '간신히'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is similar to '겨우' and '간신히', but '근근이' leans toward continuing with difficulty in hard circumstances. It goes well with '살다', '버티다', '모으다' and '이어 가다'. For barely pulling off a single thing, like just clearing a passing score, '간신히' sounds more natural.

examples.en: In recent years, one-person households have increased in every city.
The record-breaking heat of recent years became a hot topic.

examples.ko: 근년 들어 이 동네에 카페가 많이 생겼어요.
examples.en: In recent years, many cafés have opened in this neighborhood.

examples.ko: 이번 겨울은 근년에 보기 드문 추위예요.
examples.en: This winter's cold is rare for recent years.

examples.ko: 근년에는 겨울에도 눈이 거의 안 와요.
examples.en: In recent years, it hardly snows even in winter.
This road was newly paved in recent years.

explain: '요즘', '최근'과 비슷하지만 '근년'은 최근 몇 해를 말하는 글말이에요. '근년에 들어', '근년 들어'처럼 뉴스나 글에서 많이 봐요. 말할 때는 '최근 몇 년'이 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is similar to '요즘' and '최근', but '근년' refers to the last few years and belongs to written style. You often see '근년에 들어' and '근년 들어' in news and writing. In speech, '최근 몇 년' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 한국 근대사는 역사 시간에 가장 어려웠어요.
examples.en: Korean modern history was the hardest part of history class.

examples.ko: 이 박물관에서 근대사를 한눈에 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see modern history at a glance in this museum.
I watched a modern history documentary with a friend.
My father is very interested in modern history.
We had a discussion in modern history class.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 근대사의 아픔을 담고 있어요.
examples.en: This novel carries the pain of modern history.

explain: '근대'와 '현대'는 나라와 학자마다 나누는 시기가 달라요. 한국에서는 '근현대사'라고 한꺼번에 부르기도 해요. '고대사, 중세사, 근대사, 현대사'처럼 짝으로 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: Where 'modern' ends and 'contemporary' begins differs by country and scholar. In Korea people often say '근현대사' to cover both. Learn it together with '고대사', '중세사' and '현대사'.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 근대식으로 지어져서 분위기가 독특해요.
examples.en: This building was built in a modern-era style, so it has a unique atmosphere.
My grandfather is from the generation that received modern-style education.

examples.ko: 근대식 병원이 처음 생긴 때를 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned when the first modern-style hospital appeared.

examples.ko: 거리에 근대식 건물이 아직 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Some modern-era buildings still remain on the street.

examples.ko: 그 학교는 근대식 교실을 그대로 보존했어요.
examples.en: That school preserved its modern-era classroom as it was.

examples.ko: 근대식 설비를 들여와 공장을 새로 지었어요.
examples.en: They brought in modern equipment and built the factory anew.

explain: '전통식'과 반대로, 개화기 이후 서양에서 들어온 방식이나 모양을 말해요. 보통 '근대식 건물', '근대식 교육'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. '현대식'은 지금 쓰는 최신 방식이라 시기가 달라요.
explain_en: In contrast to '전통식' (traditional style), it refers to methods or looks that came from the West after the opening of the country. It is usually placed before a noun, as in '근대식 건물' and '근대식 교육'. '현대식' means today's up-to-date style, so the era is different.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 근대적인 계획에 따라 만들어졌어요.
examples.en: This city was built following a modern plan.
The modern education system began at that time.

examples.ko: 그 공장은 근대적 설비를 갖추고 있어요.
examples.en: That factory is equipped with modern facilities.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 근대적 가치관을 잘 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This novel shows modern values well.
The design of this building is very modern in style.
I was surprised that my grandmother's thinking was so modern.

explain: '근대적 + 명사'로 쓰고, '근대적이다'처럼 서술어로도 써요. '근대'는 옛날과 오늘날 사이의 시기라서, '근대적'은 '현대적'(지금 느낌)과 다르게 그 시기의 제도나 생각을 가리킬 때 써요.
explain_en: It is used before a noun as '근대적 + noun' and also as a predicate like '근대적이다'. '근대' is the period between old times and today, so '근대적' points to systems or ideas of that period, unlike '현대적', which means modern in today's sense.

examples.en: The government is trying to modernize the outdated facilities.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 짧은 기간에 산업을 근대화했어요.
examples.en: That country modernized its industry in a short time.
A project to modernize rural areas has begun.
Some people say the military needs to be modernized.

examples.ko: 이 공장은 설비를 근대화한 뒤 생산량이 늘었어요.
examples.en: After this factory modernized its equipment, output increased.

examples.ko: 학교 교육을 근대화하자고 주장한 사람들이 있었어요.
examples.en: There were people who argued for modernizing school education.

explain: '~을 근대화하다'처럼 대상이 필요한 말이에요. 사회, 산업, 제도, 시설을 옛날 방식에서 새 방식으로 바꿀 때 쓰고, 명사 '근대화'로도 많이 말해요. 공장이나 설비 이야기에서는 '현대화하다'도 같이 써요.
explain_en: It takes an object, as in '~을 근대화하다'. It is used when changing a society, industry, system or facility from an old way to a new one, and the noun '근대화' is very common too. For factories and equipment, '현대화하다' is also used.

examples.en: The approximate value of pi is 3.14.
Find an approximate value, not the exact one.

examples.ko: 계산기가 알려 준 근삿값을 노트에 적었어요.
examples.en: I wrote the approximate value the calculator gave me in my notebook.
You round off the decimals and express it as an approximate value.
This number is an approximate value, so there is some error.
I solved an approximate-value problem on the test.

explain: 수학에서 정확한 값(참값)에 가까운 값을 말해요. 표기는 '근사값'이 아니라 '근삿값'으로 써요. 일상에서 '대충 이 정도'라고 할 때는 '어림값'이나 '대략'도 써요.
explain_en: In math it means a value close to the exact (true) value. The correct spelling is '근삿값', not '근사값'. In everyday talk for a rough figure, '어림값' or '대략' is also used.

examples.en: My father worked continuously at one company for thirty years.

examples.ko: 이 회사에서 10년 이상 근속하면 휴가를 더 줘요.
examples.en: If you stay at this company for over ten years, you get extra leave.

examples.ko: 오래 근속한 직원에게 상을 주기로 했어요.
examples.en: They decided to give an award to employees who have served a long time.

examples.ko: 그분은 한 병원에서만 근속하고 싶어 했어요.
examples.en: He wanted to stay at just one hospital for his whole career.
I opened a shop with the severance pay I got after long service.
I received a gift for completing twenty years of service this year.

explain: 한 직장에서 계속 일할 때 쓰고, '근속 20년', '근속 연수'처럼 명사로도 많이 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '오래 다니다', '한 회사에 쭉 다니다'라고 해요. 보통 '20년 근속'처럼 기간과 같이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used for continuing to work at one workplace, and the noun form appears in '근속 20년' and '근속 연수' (years of service). In daily talk people say '오래 다니다' or '한 회사에 쭉 다니다'. It usually comes with a length of time, like '20년 근속'.

examples.en: Looking only at the profit in front of you is short-sighted.
That policy was criticized as short-sighted.

examples.ko: 근시안적 판단 때문에 큰 손해를 봤어요.
examples.en: We suffered a big loss because of a short-sighted decision.
A short-sighted plan won't last long.
Don't think in such a short-sighted way.
I think the team leader's decision was short-sighted.

explain: 눈이 나빠 먼 곳이 안 보이는 '근시안'에서 나온 비유로, 앞날을 보지 않고 지금만 보는 생각이나 결정을 비판할 때 써요. '근시안적 + 명사'와 '근시안적이다'를 둘 다 써요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '장기적'이에요.
explain_en: It is a figure of speech from '근시안' (a nearsighted eye), used to criticize thinking or decisions that look only at the present, not the future. Both '근시안적 + noun' and '근시안적이다' are used. The opposite idea is '장기적' (long-term).

examples.ko: 교장 선생님은 늘 근엄한 표정으로 서 계세요.
examples.en: The principal always stands with a stern expression.
My grandfather looks stern, but he is warm inside.
The king sat solemnly and looked at his subjects.

examples.ko: 그 선생님은 평소에 너무 근엄해서 말 걸기 어려워요.
examples.en: That teacher is so stern usually that it is hard to talk to him.
My great-grandfather in the photo looks very stern.
My once-stern father smiles in front of his grandchild.

explain: 엄숙하고 무게가 있어서 가까이 가기 어려운 태도에 써요. 주로 어른이나 지위 높은 사람의 표정, 목소리, 태도를 말할 때 많이 써요. '엄숙하다'는 분위기나 장소에도 쓸 수 있지만 '근엄하다'는 사람에게 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It describes a solemn, weighty manner that makes someone hard to approach. It is mostly used for the expression, voice or attitude of an elder or a person of high rank. '엄숙하다' can also describe an atmosphere or place, but '근엄하다' is used more for people.

examples.en: They are looking for the place where the fire started.
I wonder where this rumor came from.
The source of the epidemic has not been identified yet.

examples.ko: 냄새가 나는 근원지로 가 봤더니 냉장고 뒤였어요.
examples.en: I went to where the smell came from, and it was behind the fridge.

examples.ko: 근원지에서 가까울수록 소리가 더 크게 들려요.
examples.en: The closer you are to the source, the louder the sound is.
Residents near the source evacuated first.

explain: 어떤 일이나 물건이 처음 시작된 장소를 말해요. 정보가 어디서 나왔는지는 '출처'라고 하고, 강물 같은 것의 시작은 '발원지'라고 해요. '소문의 근원지', '불의 근원지'처럼 원인이 된 장소에 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means the place where something first started. Where information came from is '출처', and the start of a river is '발원지'. It is often used for the place of origin, as in '소문의 근원지' (rumor's source) or '불의 근원지' (where a fire began).

examples.en: At the root of the conflict is long-standing distrust.

examples.ko: 문제의 근저를 알아야 제대로 고칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only fix it properly if you know the root of the problem.

examples.ko: 이 이론은 근저부터 다시 생각해야 해요.
examples.en: This theory needs to be rethought from its foundation.

examples.ko: 그 말의 근저에 어떤 마음이 있는지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder what feeling lies beneath those words.

examples.ko: 근저가 튼튼하지 않으면 건물이 쉽게 흔들려요.
examples.en: If the foundation isn't solid, the building shakes easily.

examples.ko: 그의 불만은 근저에서 외로움과 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: At bottom, his complaints are tied to loneliness.

explain: '뿌리', '바탕', '밑바탕'과 비슷한 글말이에요. 주로 '근저에 깔려 있다', '근저에는 ~이/가 있다'처럼 겉으로 안 보이는 깊은 원인이나 생각을 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '밑바탕'이나 '속'이라고 많이 해요.
explain_en: It is a written-style word close to '뿌리' (root) and '밑바탕' (basis). It is mostly used in '근저에 깔려 있다' or '근저에는 ~이/가 있다' for a deep cause or idea that isn't visible on the surface. In daily talk, '밑바탕' or '속' is common.

examples.en: The spot where a mosquito bit me is itchy.
My back is itchy but I can't reach it.

examples.ko: 새 옷의 털 때문에 목이 근지러웠어요.
examples.en: My neck felt itchy because of the fuzz on the new clothes.
It itched so I scratched it, and it got even redder.
If your body feels itchy, go see a doctor.
My eyes are itchy and my nose is stuffed up.

explain: ㅂ 불규칙이라서 '근지러워요', '근지러운', '근지러웠어요'로 바뀌어요. '간지럽다'는 누가 건드려서 웃음이 날 것 같은 느낌이고, '근지럽다'는 '가렵다'처럼 긁고 싶은 느낌이라 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '근지러워요', '근지러운' and '근지러웠어요'. '간지럽다' is the ticklish feeling that makes you want to laugh when touched, whereas '근지럽다' is an itch you want to scratch, like '가렵다', so they differ.

examples.en: My arm where the mosquito bit me is itchy.
I was itching to tell the story.

examples.ko: 새 게임이 하고 싶어서 손이 근질근질해서 참을 수 없어요.
examples.en: My hands are itching to play the new game and I can't wait.

examples.ko: 근질근질 가려워서 밤새 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: It itched so much that I couldn't sleep all night.
My back is itchy, could you scratch it for me?

examples.ko: 친구가 몸이 근질근질하다고 해서 같이 달렸어요.
examples.en: My friend said he was itching to move, so we ran together.

explain: 실제 가려운 느낌뿐 아니라 무엇을 하고 싶어서 가만히 있기 어려운 마음에도 써요. 보통 '근질근질하다' 형태로 말하고, '입이/손이/몸이 근질근질하다'처럼 몸의 일부와 같이 써요. '간질간질'은 살짝 건드리는 느낌이라 달라요.

phrases.example: 비밀을 들었는데 말을 못 해서 입이 근질근질해요.
phrases.en: I heard a secret but can't tell anyone, so I'm itching to say it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말하고 싶은 마음을 참기 어려울 때 써요. 주로 비밀이나 재미있는 소식을 알고 있을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you can hardly hold back the urge to speak, usually when you know a secret or exciting news.

phrases.example: 하루 종일 앉아 있었더니 몸이 근질근질해요.
phrases.en: I've been sitting all day, so I'm itching to move.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움직이거나 운동하고 싶어서 가만히 있기 힘든 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes restlessness from wanting to move or exercise.

explain_en: Besides a literal itch, it is used for an urge to do something that makes it hard to sit still. It is usually said as '근질근질하다' and pairs with body parts, as in '입이/손이/몸이 근질근질하다'. '간질간질' is a light tickling feeling, so it is different.
